comparator.name: Earth, Climate and Technology (formerly Applied Earth Sciences)
comparator.sourceNotes: TU Delft's current programme pages, checked 2026-10-03, identify Earth, Climate and Technology as the redesigned and renamed successor to Applied Earth Sciences. The live programme page states that the formal study guide may still show Applied Earth Sciences while the official name change is processed. The current 2026-2027 curriculum chart, created in August 2026 and labelled September 2026, accounts for the complete 180 EC. The live programme description confirms four integrated learning lines: Principles of the Earth System; Earth System Data; Math, Physics and Chemistry; and Applications, Impact and Skills. Where the live prose uses a slightly different course title, the component name below follows the current 2026-2027 curriculum chart.
components: The chart presents a combined 4 + 4 EC allocation integrating applications, impact, skills and data foundations.
The chart presents a combined 4 + 4 EC allocation across the integrated Earth-system learning lines.
The chart presents a combined 4 + 4 EC allocation across the integrated physics learning lines.
The chart presents a combined 5 + 3 EC allocation across Earth-system principles and applications.
The chart presents a combined 5 + 3 EC allocation across geodata and applications.
The current curriculum chart uses this title; the live programme prose describes the corresponding solid-Earth systems and engineering content.
Genuine minor space preserved from the current programme.
Genuine specialist elective space preserved without inventing a topic.
The live programme prose describes the corresponding course as Spatiotemporal Geodata Science.
Individual research project with a written thesis and presentation.

core: Integrated Earth-system processes across subsurface, surface, water and atmosphere
Mathematics, physics, chemistry, geodata, sensing, modelling and uncertainty
Field investigation, engineering design, research and societal impact
adjacent: Subsurface resources, geothermal energy, storage and responsible extraction
Climate dynamics, environmental change, adaptation and resilience
Earth observation, spatial data and environmental monitoring
questions: How can subsurface resources and energy systems be developed responsibly?
How can field observations, sensors, satellite data and models reveal Earth and climate change?
How can technical Earth-system solutions address climate risk and environmental resilience?

alternatives.label: Earth systems, climate & environmental evidence
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines the strongest available UCR sequence in Earth science, climate, soils, water, resources, observation, quantitative methods and environmental research.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Earth, Climate and Technology: an integrated programme linking Earth processes, climate, soils, water and subsurface resources with geospatial observation, quantitative evidence and applied environmental research.
progression: Sustainability, geology, programming and mathematics precede Earth-system tools, hazards, climate, observation, soils, water, numerical methods, biogeochemistry, data analysis and advanced resource and energy applications. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; six 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Climate, sensing & geospatial data
alternatives.labelReason: This pathway gives greater weight to climate processes, signals, quantitative modelling, algorithms, Earth observation, machine learning and image-based spatial evidence.
alternatives.concept: A climate-and-observation direction organised around Earth sensing, quantitative modelling, computational analysis and geospatial evidence for environmental change and hazards.
progression: Earth science, programming and mathematical foundations precede Earth-system tools, linear algebra, numerical methods, observation, soils, machine learning, algorithms, computer vision and advanced environmental analysis. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; six 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes climate sensing and computational spatial analysis the organising priority. Relative to the closest programme it replaces biodiversity, probability, remediation and ecosystem study with linear algebra, algorithms, computer vision and nature-based engineering; the pair differs by four courses and 30 EC in each direction.

alternatives.label: Subsurface resources, energy & responsibility
alternatives.labelReason: This pathway centres subsurface science, geodata, numerical and signal analysis, resource recovery, life-cycle impacts, renewable systems and environmental responsibility.
alternatives.concept: A subsurface-resource and energy-transition direction connecting soils, aquifers, geothermal energy, carbon storage and critical resources with modelling, signals, life-cycle analysis, remediation, renewable-system design and environmental justice.
progression: Earth science, sustainability, programming and mathematical foundations precede life-cycle analysis, soils, aquifers, Earth observation, numerical and linear-system methods, biogeochemistry, remediation, data analysis, advanced resources, energy-system design and environmental justice. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes subsurface resources and the energy transition the organising priority. Relative to the closest programme it replaces biodiversity, probability, water-management and ecosystem courses with linear algebra, linear systems, life-cycle analysis, nature-based engineering and environmental justice. Relative to the climate-data route it replaces water management, algorithms and computer vision with linear systems, life-cycle analysis, remediation and environmental justice. It differs from each earlier programme by at least four courses and 30 EC in each direction.

trace: Sustainability Essentials I supplies physical, mathematical and systems foundations for studying linked environmental change.
Dynamic Earth directly examines structural geology, Earth history and environmental geology through laboratory and field work.
Introduction to Programming develops Python-based computational problem solving for environmental data and models.
Sustainability Essentials II develops integrated systems analysis for environmental and climate questions.
Mathematical Methods develops calculus, linear algebra and differential-equation techniques used in Earth-system analysis.
Natural Hazards, Risks & Adaptations applies geoscience to disasters, environmental change and adaptation.
Earth System Science Tools integrates Earth-system modelling, tracers, proxies and greenhouse-gas pathways.
Climate Change directly studies anthropogenic climate change, ocean acidification and climate adaptation.
Introduction to Biodiversity establishes biological diversity within the biosphere component of Earth systems.
Introduction to Data Science develops cleaning, visualisation and analysis of spatial and other datasets.
Probability & Statistics develops probability, distributions and parameter estimation for environmental evidence.
Earth Observation uses satellite, drone and geospatial data to measure environmental change.
Soils & Aquifers directly studies soil formation, aquifer mapping and freshwater-resource assessment.
Living with Water examines flood protection, freshwater management, land subsidence and ecological consequences.
Computational & Numerical Methods develops numerical modelling, root finding and differential-equation methods.
Environmental Biogeochemistry uses geochemical modelling to analyse waters, minerals and element cycles.
Research in a Sustainable Delta provides applied environmental research with an external partner.
R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation applies environmental chemistry and laboratory methods to resource recovery and contamination.
Machine Learning develops statistical learning methods for complex environmental and spatial datasets.
Earth’s Resources provides advanced geoscience research on geothermal energy, subsurface carbon storage, nuclear-waste storage and responsible resource use.
Governance of Sustainability examines institutions and interests shaping climate adaptation and environmental action.
Renewable System Design develops technical and economic assessment of lower-carbon energy systems through an external-company project.
Ecosystems Uncovered directly examines ecological processes and interactions between organisms and environmental conditions.
Linear Algebra supplies vector and matrix methods used in spatial modelling and data science.
Building with Nature examines ecosystem-based design, land reclamation and flood protection.
Algorithms & Data Structures develops efficient computational methods for large and complex datasets.
Image Processing & Computer Vision develops methods directly relevant to satellite and environmental imagery.
Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy evaluates environmental impacts of technologies and resource use across complete life cycles.
Linear Systems develops signal, Fourier, transfer-function and state-space methods directly relevant to the comparator’s signals and time-series spine.
Social Movements & Environmental Justice examines the justice, participation and conflict dimensions of resource extraction and environmental intervention.
blocks: Both integrate physical-science foundations, global sustainability challenges and applied problem framing.
Both develop mathematical methods used to analyse physical systems; TU Delft provides a dedicated calculus course.
Both develop vectors, matrices, linear systems and transformations.
Both develop numerical methods for modelling and simulating complex systems.
Both develop signal and systems analysis, including Fourier-based methods; TU Delft also requires dedicated time-series analysis.
UCR provides selected sustainability-science foundations but no equivalent dedicated mechanics-and-thermodynamics course.
UCR Linear Systems covers signals and transforms but not the comparator’s full electricity, magnetism, fields and waves requirement.
UCR lacks a dedicated fluid-dynamics course spanning subsurface, surface and atmospheric flow.
Both develop geological understanding through applied and field-based work; TU Delft gives greater engineering depth.
Both apply geoscience to hazards and adaptation, while TU Delft’s course is a dedicated integrated field experience.
Both integrate atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and climate through Earth-system evidence and modelling.
Both examine climate drivers, impacts, adaptation and mitigation.
Both apply chemistry to rocks, minerals, waters and environmental processes; TU Delft supplies a dedicated foundation course.
Both study advanced subsurface resources, geothermal energy and storage applications.
Both require applied technical-system design; TU Delft’s project is specific to Earth, Climate and Technology engineering.
UCR studies climate and environmental change but lacks a dedicated atmosphere-and-ocean dynamics course.
Both examine interacting water, surface and climate processes; TU Delft includes more physical atmospheric science.
Both examine how environmental and technical choices interact with governance and society.
Geodata, sensing, field research and choice
Both develop data preparation, visualisation and analysis; TU Delft adds specialised geodetic measurement.
Both develop image and spatial-data analysis relevant to remote sensing.
Both use spatial and temporal geodata to investigate environmental change.
Both use collaborative applied research on a real environmental problem; TU Delft requires a larger international field project.
The genuine 30-EC minor space is preserved without invented content.
The genuine specialist elective is preserved without inventing a topic.
TU Delft requires an individual 15-EC bachelor thesis; UCR’s standardized optional independent-research opportunity is presented alongside it.

notes.text: TU Delft prescribes mechanics, thermodynamics, chemistry, fields and waves, fluid dynamics, atmosphere and ocean dynamics, geological engineering, geodata, international fieldwork, engineering design and a 15-EC thesis. UCR can build substantial Earth-system, climate, soils, water, resources, observation and quantitative pathways, but it does not reproduce that complete engineering-physics and field-project sequence.

selection.assessment: The closest programme covers integrated Earth systems, climate, soils, water, resources, geospatial evidence and research. Climate sensing/geospatial analysis and subsurface resources/energy responsibility form two further independently evidenced, coherent and mechanically feasible directions. All three pass the pairwise 30-EC distinctness floor, so production stops at the maximum.
